big_case.notes: Independent read: a genuine, respondent-conceded six-circuit split on whether an officer may open a hash-matched CyberTip file without a warrant, governing a nationwide investigative pipeline; a grant would have been a significant Fourth Amendment case. But the vehicle was an interlocutory state criminal suppression ruling with a facial section 1257 finality problem, one amicus, no CVSG, and the Court denied silently after one full conference. Big issue, modest case. Disclosure: I printed the staged prediction.json files whole before writing, so the predictors' big_case_score values were visible before I fixed this number; the read above is formed from the record, not from them.

leakage.notes: Forward cell: prediction created 2026-09-16 from the 2026-09-15 snapshot; the denial came 2026-10-05, so the case was genuinely open. Log: 24 calls, every one `unobserved` (result_capture_coverage 0.0, the engine's standing shape), so each is graded on its query: file reads and directory listings of the provisioned record, greps of the petition and BIO for 'split', a read of metrics/statpack.md, one `fedcourts query` with structured era/disposition filters, and the output writes. No web search, no CourtListener call, no query naming this petition's disposition, no retrieved_doc_date. Nothing outcome-revealing was sought. Minor self-report inconsistency, not leakage: retrieval.md says no retrieval beyond provisioned inputs, but the log carries one corpus query call.
